fullPassage: In the early 1960s the great American writer James Baldwin wrote: “People are trapped in history, and history is trapped in them.” He was speaking to race when he penned those words. But the statement is equally true if the word “people” is replaced with “all of life on Earth, present and past,” for each strand of DNA, in each of our cells, is an ancient record of biological history, written in simple code and passed down from generation to generation. One could say that DNA is nothing but history, one with a physical manifestation that was slowly blended and accumulated over countless eons by the most pitiless of all phenomena — natural selection. DNA is a history that is inside us — and yet one that is our master as well, the blueprint for our bodies, and dictator of what we will pass on to our children, gifts that can be blessings — or deadly time bombs. We are indeed trapped in this particular vehicle of history as much as it is trapped in us.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) equally=동등하게, (B) replaced=대체된, (C) passed=전해진
det.analysis:
❌ ① barely — replaced — passed: (A) barely(거의 ~않게)는 equally(동등하게)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② equally — distorted — passed: (B) distorted(왜곡된)는 replaced(대체된)와 의미가 달라 부적절
✅ ③ equally — replaced — passed: 원문 일치. 동등하게(equally) 참이고, 대체되면(replaced), 세대로 전해진(passed) ←정답
❌ ④ equally — replaced — blocked: (C) blocked(차단된)는 passed(전해진)의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: equally true = 동등하게 참이다 / replaced with = ~로 대체하다 / passed down = 전해지다

But the statement is equally true if the word “people” is <u>replaced</u> with “all of life on Earth, present and past,” for each strand of DNA, in each of our cells, is an ancient record of biological history, written in simple code and passed down from generation to generation. One could say that DNA is nothing but history, one with a physical manifestation that was slowly blended and accumulated over countless eons by the most pitiless of all phenomena — natural selection. DNA is a history that is inside us — and yet one that is our master as well, the blueprint for our bodies, and dictator of what we will pass on to our children, gifts that can be blessings — or deadly time bombs. We are indeed trapped in this particular vehicle of history as much as it is trapped in us.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 replaced와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: replaced = 대체된. 반의어는 '유지된/보존된'
det.analysis:
✅ ① retained: 유지된/보존된 → replaced(대체된)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ② exchanged: 교환된 → replaced의 유의어
❌ ③ substituted: 대체된 → replaced의 유의어
❌ ④ altered: 변경된 → replaced와 유사한 의미
det.tip: replaced(대체된) ↔ retained(유지된). retained = 바꾸지 않고 그대로 보존한

questions.passage:
(A) He was <u>speaking</u> to race when he penned those words, addressing the long history of racial injustice in America.
(B) The data <u>speaks</u> for itself — the results clearly show that the experiment was successful.
questions.stem: 다음 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 speak의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) speak to = ~에 대해 언급/논하다 / (B) speak for itself = 스스로를 증명하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① 말하다 — 증명하다: (A)에서 speak to는 단순 '말하다'가 아니라 특정 주제를 '언급하다'
❌ ② 연설하다 — 말하다: (A)는 연설이 아닌 언급, (B)는 말하다가 아닌 증명하다
✅ ③ 언급하다 — 증명하다: (A) speaking to race = 인종 문제를 언급하다, (B) speaks for itself = 스스로 증명하다 ←정답
❌ ④ 연설하다 — 증명하다: (A)는 연설이 아닌 '~에 대해 언급하다'
det.tip: speak to = ~에 대해 언급하다 (address) / speak for itself = 자명하다, 스스로 증명하다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "an absolute ruler who exercises power harshly; one who determines or controls what others must do"

det.korean: 절대 권력을 행사하는 통치자; 다른 이의 행동을 결정하는 사람 = dictator(독재자)
det.analysis:
❌ ① blueprint: 설계도 → 구조를 보여주는 도면이지 통치자가 아님
❌ ② phenomenon: 현상 → 관찰 가능한 사건이지 권력 행사자가 아님
❌ ③ vehicle: 매개체 → 운반 수단이지 통치자가 아님
✅ ④ dictator: 독재자 → 절대 권력을 행사하는 통치자 ←정답
det.tip: dictator = 독재자. DNA가 '무엇을 물려줄지 결정하는 독재자(dictator)' 역할
